title: Common JSON Errors and How to Validate Them
author: Reconnect Master
description: Clarifying the confusion between JSON and JavaScript—they're related but fundamentally different.
A beginner-friendly guide to common JSON syntax errors, validation methods, their limitations, and useful terminal commands for different operating systems.

content.heading: 1. Common JSON Errors
content.paragraph: JSON is a data format with strict syntax rules. Even a small mistake can prevent a website from reading or loading the data correctly. Here are some common errors beginners may encounter:

list.description: JSON requires Double Quotes (") for both Keys and String Values. Single Quotes (') are not allowed.
Do not add a comma after the last item before closing an Object (}) or Array (]).
Forgetting to add a comma (,) between data items will cause a syntax error.
Standard JSON does not support comments such as // or /* */.

content.heading: 2. Ways to Validate JSON
content.paragraph: There are two main ways to check whether your JSON code is valid:

methods.name: JSON Validator
methods.description: Tools such as JSONLint help check whether JSON follows the correct syntax rules. They identify errors and indicate their locations, such as the line and column numbers.
methods.use_case: Useful for validating JSON files online or when a code editor such as VS Code is unavailable.

methods.name: Code Editor (VS Code)
methods.description: VS Code has a built-in JSON validation feature. It highlights syntax errors with red squiggly lines and displays error messages as you write.
methods.additional_feature: You can also view all detected errors in the Problems panel.

content.heading: 3. Limitations of JSON Validator
content.paragraph: A JSON Validator checks only the structure and syntax according to JSON rules. It cannot determine whether a Key is spelled correctly or matches the requirements of the JavaScript code that uses the data.

example.explanation: The Key "titel" is still valid JSON because its syntax is correct. However, the website may fail to retrieve the data if JavaScript expects a Key named "title".

content.conclusion: Therefore, if you want to verify both data accuracy and compatibility with your application, you need to check the code further rather than relying on a JSON Validator alone.
